one_line: A Tamil Shaiva poet-saint and a Pallava ruler in early Bhakti-era Tamil country, mid-7th century CE.

appearance.age_look: Appar appears as a lean man in his late 50s; Mahendravarman as a broad-shouldered king in his early 30s.
appearance.face: Appar has a gently lined oval face, medium-brown Tamil complexion, calm eyes with a soft smile and a white horizontal sacred ash streak on his forehead; Mahendravarman has a square jaw, slightly lighter brown complexion, sharp confident eyes and a small neatly trimmed moustache, usually with a composed, dignified expression.
appearance.hair: Appar’s hair is dark, pulled back into a modest low knot at the nape, with a thin white cloth band around his head; Mahendravarman’s hair is thick and dark, combed back into a short, tidy topknot partially covered by a simple golden Pallava-style coronet band with a small central leaf-shaped ornament.
appearance.costume: Appar wears a plain, ankle-length off-white cotton veshti (dhoti) wrapped securely and pleated in front, with a soft light-ochre cotton angavastram draped from left shoulder across the torso and around the back; he has simple wooden bead malas at his neck and wrist and thin leather sandals. Mahendravarman wears a finely woven cream-coloured ankle-length dhoti with a broad maroon border, tied high and neat, and a fitted short-sleeved pale gold tunic that reaches mid-thigh, decorated with subtle woven geometric motifs near the hem; a deep maroon silk uttariya (shawl) with a thin gold edge is draped from his right shoulder across his chest; he has a wide gold waist-belt, modest gold armlets and wrist bangles, and sturdy brown leather sandals suitable for palace and temple visits.
appearance.signature: Appar carries a simple, smooth wooden walking staff in his right hand and a small palm-leaf manuscript bundle tied with string at his waist; Mahendravarman carries a rolled palm-leaf inscription scroll in his left hand as his symbol of royal patronage and temple-building.

ref_desc: Appar is a lean older Tamil man with a low hair knot, off-white dhoti and light-ochre shawl carrying a wooden staff, while Mahendravarman is a younger Pallava king with a coronet, cream dhoti, gold tunic, maroon shawl and palm-leaf scroll, in off-white, ochre, cream, maroon and gold tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw an anime-style full-body character sheet of two figures side by side: Appar and Mahendravarman I from early Pallava Tamil country. Appar is a lean older Tamil man with a gently lined oval face, medium-brown complexion, calm eyes, and a white horizontal sacred ash streak on his forehead, his dark hair pulled back into a modest low knot with a thin white cloth band. He wears an ankle-length off-white cotton dhoti wrapped and pleated in front, a soft light-ochre cotton shawl draped from his left shoulder across his torso, simple wooden bead malas at neck and wrist, and thin leather sandals; he holds a smooth wooden walking staff in his right hand and a small tied bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts at his waist. Mahendravarman I stands beside him as a broad-shouldered young Pallava king with a square jaw, slightly lighter brown complexion, sharp confident eyes, and a small neatly trimmed moustache, his thick dark hair combed back into a short topknot partially covered by a simple golden coronet band with a small central leaf-shaped ornament. He wears a finely woven cream ankle-length dhoti with a broad maroon border, a pale gold short-sleeved tunic down to mid-thigh with subtle woven geometric motifs at the hem, and a deep maroon silk shawl with a thin gold edge draped from his right shoulder across his chest, along with a wide gold waist-belt, modest gold armlets and bangles, and sturdy brown leather sandals. He carries a rolled palm-leaf inscription scroll in his left hand as his symbol of royal patronage. Use a harmonious palette of off-white, light ochre, cream, maroon and gold, and show them front, three-quarter, and back views to clearly display face, hair, clothing details, and their signature staff and scroll.
